item.title: Xi puts forward four-point proposal at SCO Bishkek summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Xi puts forward four-point proposal at SCO Bishkek summit BISHKEK -- President Xi Jinping on Tuesday put forward a four-point proposal at the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) in the Kyrgyz capital of Bishkek. In his speech at the summit, Xi said this year marks the 25th founding anniversary of the SCO. He pointed out that 25 years ago, safeguarding sovereignty, security and development interests became a shared consensus among countries in the region in the face of the profound lessons of the Cold War, the real threat posed by the "three evil forces," as well as the strong aspirations of people in various countries for peace and development. The SCO thus emerged, and the organization has increasingly demonstrated its strong vitality and dynamism, Xi added. Over the past 25 years, the SCO has gone through an extraordinary journey, Xi said, noting that its most significant achievement has been its gradual transformation into a new type of regional cooperation organization that spans the largest geographical area, represents the largest population, and possesses enormous development potential in the world. The SCO's most valuable spiritual asset is the pioneering proposal and steadfast adherence to the "Shanghai Spirit" of mutual trust, mutual benefit, equality, consultation, respect for the diversity of civilizations, and pursuit of common development, he said. The SCO's most important experience for cooperation is that it has found the right way of coexistence featuring non-alliances, non-confrontation and not targeting any third party, while bringing countries in the region together to build a common home, he added. Xi said that 25 years on, as profound changes unseen in a century are accelerating, the rivalry is intensifying between dialogue and confrontation, win-win cooperation and zero-sum games, and multilateralism and unilateralism, and the shadow of war continues to haunt the world. At the crossroads concerning the future of humanity, the SCO should shoulder its historic responsibility and take the initiative in steering the course of history, he said. Xi called on the SCO to stay committed to putting development first, and open up the prospects for shared prosperity. The SCO, Xi said, should champion a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, consolidate cooperation in traditional areas such as trade and investment, connectivity, energy and resources, and expand cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, digital economy, green industry and green mining. China sees the SCO as a priority area for the high-quality joint construction of the Belt and Road and implementation of the Global Development Initiative, and will continue to host events such as the SCO Digital Economy Forum and the SCO Agricultural Expo, Xi said. China will also establish an international cooperation center on AI applications for SCO countries, set up a China-SCO port economy cooperation center in Tianjin, and jointly implement 100 technological cooperation projects with SCO countries over the next three years, Xi added. Xi urged the SCO to stay committed to taking security as a key goal, and foster an environment of common security.

item.title: CXMT surging forward in memory race
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
CXMT surging forward in memory race Chinese chipmaker's DRAM to debut in Xiaomi's upcoming foldable Chinese memory-chip maker ChangXin Memory Technologies is moving closer to a vanguard position amid the global DRAM race with one of the earliest commercial deployments of LPDDR6 in a flagship smartphone, industry experts said on Monday. They made the comments as CXMT said on Saturday that it had begun mass production of its self-developed LPDDR6 DRAM, which will debut in Xiaomi's upcoming 18 Fold handset. The chip has a peak data-transfer rate of 12,800 megabits per second and capacity of up to 16 gigabytes. "For a Chinese company that only began mass-producing its first DRAM products in 2019, the bigger significance is not simply being first with one product," said Wang Peng, a researcher at the Beijing Academy of Social Sciences. "It put CXMT into the first wave of competition around the latest mobile-memory standard alongside global heavyweights Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology," Wang said. LPDDR6 is designed to raise memory bandwidth and parallelism while cutting power consumption, with these features becoming increasingly important as artificial intelligence models migrate from cloud data centers into phones, PCs, cars and other modalities. The Xiaomi partnership adds another dimension. It puts a Chinese-designed mobile processor and the country's newest-generation DRAM together inside a premium smartphone. Xiaomi founder and CEO Lei Jun said the company's Xring O3 would support CXMT's LPDDR6, and he expects deeper collaboration among Chinese tech companies. Advanced chips require years of engineering but also large-scale customer validation to improve yields, reliability and costs. China's huge base of smartphone, computer, electric vehicle and internet companies can give local chipmakers something laboratory breakthroughs alone cannot provide — millions of devices on which new technology can be tested and refined, industry experts said. Liu Zhiying, a professor at the University of Science and Technology of China, said, "An important factor in the growth of Chinese high-tech companies is their ability to connect research, commercialization and market applications, allowing leading companies to pull suppliers across the industrial chain forward." CXMT's technological progress is arriving alongside a dramatic expansion in its financial firepower. On Monday, shares of CXMT closed at 58.01 yuan ($8.6), down 1.01 percent on the day, valuing the company at about 3.94 trillion yuan and making it one of China's most valuable listed companies. The company recently reported first-half revenue of 150.31 billion yuan, up about 874 percent from a year earlier, while net profit attributable to shareholders reached 77.61 billion yuan, reversing a 2.33 billion yuan loss a year earlier. The surge was driven by sharply higher memory prices and rising sales as demand for computing power tightened global DRAM supplies, the company said. CXMT has grown into the world's fourth-largest DRAM producer, behind Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron, turning China from a marginal player in memory chips into an increasingly consequential competitor. Last week, CXMT sued the US Department of Defense in federal court in Washington, seeking removal from a Pentagon list of companies alleged to have ties to China's military. CXMT said its chips are designed primarily for civilian and commercial use and that it has no affiliation with the Chinese military. It said the designation was unsupported by facts and had damaged its reputation and business interests since it was first placed on the Pentagon's blacklist in January 2025. The lawsuit follows similar legal challenges by Chinese companies including Xiaomi and WuXi AppTec. Xiaomi successfully challenged an earlier Pentagon military designation in 2021. Zhang Sinan, an independent commentator who has been following the situation, said, "The US can keep extending the list, but the world will not stop needing cheaper clean energy, more efficient electric vehicles, more advanced drug development services or more flexible robotic applications simply because of a list." chengyu@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: For villagers, life continues in temporary shelter
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
For villagers, life continues in temporary shelter Around 8 am on Monday, Kelsang Palmo began packing luggage for her son, who was about to start junior high school in the Gyirong county seat, about 70 kilometers away. She stuffed a backpack with homemade Tibetan flatbread, apples, packaged cakes, cold medication and a thermos, along with a suitcase containing winter clothing and other daily necessities. After a mudslide struck Gyirong Port in the Xizang autonomous region on Wednesday morning, Kelsang Palmo and her family from Kopa village, near the hardest-hit border crossing, were relocated to a hotel to avoid secondary disasters. Despite the disruption caused by the mudslide, authorities have tried to maintain a sense of normalcy for local villagers, allowing the rituals and rhythms of daily life to continue. Kelsang Palmo's son was among five children staying at the hotel who were picked up by an arranged vehicle around noon on Monday and taken to junior high school. Throughout the morning, doors were left open as neighbors popped in and out of rooms, offering khata — silk scarves traditionally presented when welcoming or seeing off guests — to the children. "In our tradition, each household also gives departing students some pocket money — maybe 5 to 10 yuan ($0.74 to $1.48) — as a blessing, and also so that they have some change to buy snacks while away from home," said Karma, head of Kopa village. The temporary shelter at the hotel provides free accommodation, including three meals a day, as well as medical care and psychological support, for about 120 relocated residents from Kopa and Trungsi villages. "We also have a group of volunteers helping address their needs. These past few days, some have accompanied parents who are not familiar with this area to nearby stores to purchase items such as winter jackets for their children," Karma said. As relocated villagers are unable to tend to their cattle, chickens or crops at home, several officials have also remained in the village to help with poultry and farm work. "They stay in facilities that have passed safety inspections, and we are constantly monitoring local environmental conditions to ensure their safety as well," Karma said. Butri and her brother, Migmar, were both excited to start the new semester. "I really like the free meals provided here, especially the white rice," Migmar said. "But I am also looking forward to visiting the school because I've never been there." Butri said she was keen to meet her new classmates and kick shuttlecock with them. While life continues, traces of the disaster remain visible. The thumping of helicopters flying overhead can be heard constantly at the hotel. Residents have also put their favorite pastime of dancing and singing on hold out of respect for those who lost their lives in the mudslide. Sangmo, mother of the siblings, occasionally scrolled through video clips of the mudslide sweeping down the area. She did not see the waves of mud and ice herself, but she remembers hearing a deafening sound at the time. "It was horrifying," she said. "Our life here is nice, but I also miss my home." Contact the writers at wangxiaoyu@chinadaily.com.cn

With ties between China and Arab countries growing ever closer, language is playing an increasingly important role in connecting people and creating new opportunities. In Shishi, Fujian province, a free Arabic language program is helping Chinese merchants overcome language barriers and expand their reach into Arab markets. Across the Arab world, growing access to Chinese language education is opening new pathways to education, employment and deeper cultural exchange. Language is building bridges, turning dialogue into understanding and connections into lasting friendships.

item.title: Peng attends event for spouses of leaders during SCO summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Peng Liyuan attends event for spouses of leaders during SCO summit BISHKEK -- Peng Liyuan, wife of President Xi Jinping, attended on Tuesday morning an event organized by Aigul Japarova, wife of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov, for spouses of leaders attending the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit 2026. Upon arriving at the Ala-Archa State Residence, Peng was warmly greeted by Japarova. Peng and spouses of leaders from relevant countries viewed an exhibition on the ethnic culture of Kyrgyzstan and posed for group photos, before watching a stage performance at the Enesay Reception House. Peng said the performance was wonderful and praised the performers for their outstanding artistry. She extended invitations to artists of Kyrgyzstan to visit China for more performances and cultural exchanges so as to give Chinese audiences a closer look at the country's rich ethnic culture.

item.title: Consolidating mutual trust with Mongolia stressed
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Consolidating mutual trust with Mongolia stressed President Xi Jinping called on China and Mongolia to consolidate strategic mutual trust, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation and strengthen the bonds between their peoples, during a meeting with Mongolian President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, on Monday. The two sides should inject greater vitality into their comprehensive strategic partnership and advance the building of a China-Mongolia community with a shared future, Xi said. Peaceful coexistence, mutual support and win-win cooperation have always been the defining features of bilateral relations, Xi said, adding that China will continue to place ties with Mongolia high on the agenda of its neighborhood diplomacy. Xi stressed the need for the two countries to consolidate the political foundation of their relationship, and respect each other's independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity. Xi also called on the two sides to strengthen coordination and collaboration in multilateral affairs and jointly address global challenges. Khurelsukh said that deepening friendly cooperation with China is a top priority of Mongolia's foreign policy, while reaffirming his country's firm commitment to the one-China principle. Mongolia is willing to work with China to advance the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity, he added.

item.title: Relationship with Uzbekistan ushers in 'golden decade'
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Relationship with Uzbekistan ushers in 'golden decade' President Xi Jinping expressed on Monday China's readiness to work with Uzbekistan to consolidate strategic mutual trust, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation and usher in a new "golden decade" for bilateral relations. Xi made the remarks during a meeting with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. This year marks the 10th anniversary of the China-Uzbekistan comprehensive strategic partnership. Xi emphasized the improvement and upgrading of bilateral ties, the fruitful outcomes of bilateral cooperation in various areas, and the achievements in the building of the China-Uzbekistan community with a shared future. He called on the two countries to advance the high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, expand cooperation in artificial intelligence and desertification control, and pursue win-win outcomes. As founding members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, China and Uzbekistan should work together to implement the outcomes of last year's Tianjin summit and promote regional development and prosperity, he added. Mirziyoyev said that Uzbekistan is firmly committed to developing relations with China and stands ready to work with China to deepen political mutual trust, expand trade and investment, and promote people-to-people exchanges. zhoujin@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Momentum of strong ties with Russia hailed
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
Momentum of strong ties with Russia hailed Exchanges and cooperation between China and Russia have maintained a dynamic momentum of development, President Xi Jinping said on Monday when meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. In May, Putin made a successful state visit to China. Xi noted that he and Putin had made arrangements from a strategic, long-term perspective to take bilateral relations to a higher quality and a higher level of development. They also reached consensus on deepening cooperation across various fields under new circumstances. Both countries' relevant authorities are actively implementing the consensus and have already achieved many outcomes, Xi said. He expressed confidence that under their strategic guidance and through joint efforts, the foundation of the relationship will become more solid, progress will be steadier, and prospects will be brighter. Putin noted that bilateral cooperation has developed rapidly. Russia is willing to maintain high-level exchanges with China, strengthen cooperation in areas such as trade, energy, industry, transportation, and science and technology, and enhance people-to-people exchanges, he said. Speaking on the international situation, Xi said currently changes unseen in a century are accelerating, and uncertainties and unforeseeable factors in the international landscape have markedly increased. However, pursuit of peace, development, cooperation and win-win outcomes by peoples around the world remains unchanged, he said. The SCO shoulders the mission of maintaining regional stability and promoting development, he said. Putin said Russia and China should continuously strengthen unity and cooperation within the SCO and play a leading role.
